header: Date: 2026-08-26 | Time: 14:00-14:45 UTC | Duration: 45 minutes\nAttendees (Redwood): Maya Chen (AE), Liam O'Connor (SE), Priya Rao (CSM)\nAttendees (Orion Synergy): Evan Brooks (Channel Lead), Sofia Martinez (Head of Partnerships), Noah Kim (Solutions Architect), Lara Voss (Sales)
summary: Quarterly partner co-sell pipeline review focused on alignment for six high-priority joint accounts, co-sell plays, responsibilities, and next steps to run pilot POCs for two strategic customers. Discussed competitive positioning and technical benchmarks. Agreed on deliverables: playbook, benchmarks, account list, and exec briefing scheduling.
topics: Executive sponsor outreach and joint deck
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the pipeline.
[00:10] Evan Brooks: Evan here.
[00:12] Sofia Martinez: Sofia, hi.
[00:15] Noah Kim: Noah here.
[00:17] Lara Voss: Lara in for sales.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: Liam from Redwood SE.
[00:23] Priya Rao: Priya from CSM.
[00:26] Maya Chen: Great, thanks. Agenda — top six joint accounts, two pilots, technical benchmarking, and next steps. Evan, do you want to kick off with the account list?
[00:38] Evan Brooks: Yeah sure. So we've pulled together six accounts we think are ripe for co-sell: DeltaFin, Meridian Health, Atlas Logistics, Greenleaf Retail, Borealis Energy, and Nova Systems. The top three — DeltaFin and Meridian — are where we've got executive access. DeltaFin is the highest priority.
[00:58] Sofia Martinez: To add, DeltaFin has a hard timeline, they're aiming to launch a customer-facing summarization feature by Q1. So timing's tight.
[01:08] Maya Chen: That helps. For DeltaFin — we'd propose a dedicated pilot to show latency and cost profiles on their typical work load. Liam, can you outline what we'd need for the benchmark?
[01:19] Liam O'Connor: Sure. For a meaningful bench we'll need sample prompt sets, average sequence lengths, token expectations, and request rates. Ideally a small dataset of representative transcripts or documents. We'll run Redwood hosted plus dedicated config comparisons — quantized models vs FP16 — and capture p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:40] Noah Kim: Quick question — any chance we can use approximate numbers without sharing PII? DeltaFin is sensitive.
[01:48] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. We can work with anonymized or synthetic datasets that mimic size/complexity. Also we can run tests in Orion's VPC if you prefer private env — but that adds setup time.
[01:59] Evan Brooks: Good to know. For timeline, we want bench results within two weeks ideally. Is that realistic?
[02:06] Liam O'Connor: Two weeks is tight but doable for a basic bench if you can share datasets this week. For VPC/on-prem it's typically 3-4 weeks.
[02:15] Maya Chen: Ok we'll capture that as an action item — Evan to confirm dataset approach.
[02:20] Lara Voss: On the pricing front, are we aligned on the co-sell split? We've been doing 70/30 for net new ARR historically but some of these are expansion.
[02:31] Priya Rao: From Redwood ops perspective, we can be flexible. For new logos we typically support competitive intro discounts for the first 3-6 months. We'll need a joint pricing sheet though.
[02:40] Maya Chen: I'll send an updated co-sell playbook that includes suggested splits and an example pricing proposal.
[02:45] Sofia Martinez: Great. Also thinking about roles — Orion will lead outreach to product and procurement, Redwood will lead technical engagement. Does that match your expectation?
[02:55] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood AE/SE handle the technical sell and demos, Orion owns channel intro and exec sponsor outreach. We'll map account owners in the playbook.
[03:05] Evan Brooks: For the two pilots — DeltaFin and Meridian Health — what's the suggested scope?
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: DeltaFin: end-user summarization, throughput up to 500 qps peak for a short window, latency target p95 < 400ms. Meridian: internal clinical note summarization, strict data controls, needs SOC 2 and SSO compliance, preference for private deployment or dedicated.
[03:31] Noah Kim: About Meridian — they will require an audit trail and KMS integration if we touch PHI. Can Redwood support HSM/KMS?
[03:39] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS integrations; we have audit logs and can discuss SOC 2 artifacts. I'll attach security docs.
[03:46] Evan Brooks: Perfect. On competitive positioning — we've seen Anthropic and Vertex come up. How do we frame Redwood?
[03:54] Maya Chen: We position Redwood as production-first inference — predictable latency, cost controls, dedicated pools, and VPC/private options. For customers worried about vendor lock or model updates, we emphasize model pinning and rollouts. Liam, can you add the perf/quantization angle?
[04:08] Liam O'Connor: Sure — our runtime supports kernel selection and quantization-friendly paths. In practice that means similar quality with lower cost in many workloads; we'll show examples in the benchmark sheet. Also we can set up fallback policies to cheaper model variants if capacity is constrained.
[04:23] Lara Voss: One objection we often hear is "we already use OpenAI for prototypes" — what's the ask to move forward?
[04:31] Maya Chen: The ask is twofold: run a short pilot that demonstrates comparable quality but better unit economics and controls, and get a sponsor to sign off on a 6-12 month reserved capacity if results are positive.
[04:43] Evan Brooks: Let's talk logistics for the pilot — who signs MSA? Does Orion sign as channel partner or does Redwood sign directly with customers?
[04:53] Sofia Martinez: We usually require a partner-led agreement for co-sell, but client contracting can be direct with Redwood if customers prefer. We'll surface that per-account.
[05:01] Maya Chen: We'll include contract flow options in the playbook.
[05:05] Noah Kim: Quick tech interjection — for DeltaFin's workload they use longer context windows (~4k tokens). Does Redwood support that without big latency penalties?
[05:15] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we optimize kernels by seq length distribution. 4k is supported; the benchmark will show p50/p95. For really long contexts we recommend KV caching to avoid re-encoding.
[05:27] Evan Brooks: Good. Any blockers from Orion's side?
[05:30] Evan Brooks: Primary blocker is aligning our GTM heads and confirming account owners. Also need clarity on co-sell econs.
[05:37] Maya Chen: Actionable: Evan to confirm account owners and dataset approach. Maya to send playbook and pricing. Liam to send benchmark template. Priya to set up joint Slack and invite execs.
[05:49] Sofia Martinez: One more thing — do we have a joint one-pager or deck we can use for exec outreach?
[05:55] Maya Chen: We have a partner co-sell deck; I'll tailor a joint version for Orion and share.
[06:01] Lara Voss: Timeline — we'd like to kick pilots by mid-September. Is that feasible?
[06:07] Liam O'Connor: If we start bench right away and use hosted tests, yes. VPC/dedicated will push dates out.
[06:13] Evan Brooks: Let's aim for mid-September hosted pilot, Meridian may require private so later.
[06:19] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Anything else on risks or compliance?
[06:24] Noah Kim: Meridian's procurement will ask for data residency controls — that's a potential showstopper if not addressed.
[06:32] Priya Rao: We have region options and Private deployment; suggest we document the residency approach in the playbook for Meridian.
[06:40] Sofia Martinez: Okay. For competitive intel — are there any deals where we need to push special pricing to beat Anthropic?
[06:46] Maya Chen: We'll evaluate per-account. For DeltaFin we can offer a time-limited introductory rate in the playbook.
[06:53] Evan Brooks: Last thing: exec briefing — let's schedule a 30-minute briefing with our VP Partnerships and Redwood's Head of Sales. Week of Sept 6 works.
[07:01] Maya Chen: I'll propose times after the call.
[07:04] Liam O'Connor: I'll follow up with the benchmark sheet and a short tech note on model suggestions and quantization options.
[07:11] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll recap next steps in an email and update the CRM.
[07:16] Evan Brooks: Thanks all.
[07:18] Sofia Martinez: Thanks.
[07:19] End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: some speaker labels may be off; minor word errors present (e.g., "quantization" heard as "quantization", proper nouns slightly off).

Targets: datasets shared this week, benchmarks within two weeks for hosted tests, exec briefing week of 2026-09-06.
